items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-02
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...told me about people like Joe Avery and Wilbur Tillman.

ctx.x: No, this was, they sort of flowered and whelped it before I came on the scene.

Well, in 45, I used to go up there and I would write a letter, and she answered it and told me the names of a lot of the old-time musicians who were in New Orleans, and like, well, Johnny Saint Cyr and Monk Hazel, which Monk was a particular kind to me. Really? Yeah, I've been, and told me about people like Joe Avery and Wilbur Tillman. I mean, well, there was segregation and everything. It didn't mean that the white musicians didn't listen to the blacks and vice versa. They knew each other, and probably played…

You know, I don't remember. Let's see. Well, there were, the first one I went to was in a place, I don't recall, was in some, some nightclub, I believe, but I don't have any recollection of what, where it had been.

items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-07-31
items.q: I went to your, Joe Avery and Wilbur Tillman's band

ctx.x: It was on General Ogden, just off of, off of Metairie Road, where Metairie Road was at the time. Yeah.

Well, Alvin Alcorn still lives in the 1600s, like a general Ogden. I mean, that happened to remind me of, you know, and there used to be parades all over. And I, God knows how we found out about those. I honestly did not have any idea of who first told me about parades. I suppose it was 1945, I went to your, Joe Avery and Wilbur Tillman's band, and they told me about it. But I couldn't go, because I think I had to get back to the Navy base. But we sure did go to a fair number of them. Yeah. With different bands.…
I was born in Hotel Dew in New Orleans on February 25th, 1927.
